limitations: A plain PostgreSQL logical restore does not recreate Supabase-managed Auth/platform state or Storage object bytes.

The Supabase Vault extension is not present in the current local PostgreSQL 16.2 package. The previous staging restore excluded the Vault schema/extension explicitly; this did not validate Vault decryption.

Production currently has zero Vault secret rows, so this baseline contains no existing Vault ciphertext to decrypt. The root key was not exported, so any future/non-empty secret inventory still requires the owner-approved key recovery process and compatible extension.
Do not claim complete Supabase recovery from a restore that omits managed Auth, Storage objects, or any non-empty Vault inventory.
notes: Read-only production query on 2026-10-16 found zero rows in vault.secrets. There are no existing application Vault ciphertext rows to recover in this baseline.
Supabase Vault 0.3.1 remains installed; the project encryption root key was not exported. This is a dependency for future Vault secrets and decryption, not a current non-empty-secret restore blocker.

The tenant secret migration calls vault.create_secret only when a legacy organizations.gemini_api_key value is nonblank. Production is still on the pre-tenant schema where organizations is absent; the reviewed Wamule tenant seed leaves that key unset. Recheck Vault row count immediately before and after migration rehearsal.
pgcrypto 1.3 is installed. pgsodium is not installed. A read-only scan found no business-defined SQL functions referencing pgp encryption/decryption, pgsodium, or Vault calls.

Supabase Auth encrypted fields and managed Auth state are platform-managed dependencies, separate from application Vault secret rows. A logical database restore does not recreate the Auth service configuration or users.
